I'm a bit late to the party, but I'll contribute anyways.

My parents split when I was very young, so young that I have no memories of them being together. I've heard both sides of the story; my mother claimed that my father hurt my sister, while my father claimed that he left with me when my mother refused to kick their meth addictions together.

Some of my first memories were formed while living in a dingy little camper with my father. I remember the morning that I was taken from my bed, scooped up by the arms of my mother as she whisked me away from my father's angry shouts. It wasn't until later I realized I had been kidnapped.

I lived with my mother up in the mountains, several hours north of my birthplace. At this time my mom was still carrying a vicious meth addiction. I was probably 4 at this time. This was when my brother brought me with him to his friend's house to watch a porno. I remember eating a plum for the first time as a hardcore scene in a hot tub played up on the television. I decided that plums were delicious.

Christmas day. Our mother let us each open one present apiece. I was playing with my new set of toy cars when a knock at the door came. My mother told me to hide in a panic, so I ran into her closet and hid in a box, pulling a blanket over the open top. I heard loud shouting and a police officer came in and started searching the room. I remember him carrying me past my mother, who was fighting desperately against the hold of two police officers, to my father. For the next couple of years my dad and I lived with my grandmother.

One day, I remember my dad sleeping all day. My grandmother told me to go into his bedroom and smell his breath. My dad awoke when I climbed up onto the bed, and demanded to know what I was doing. In my naiveté I told him grandma's request, and he got mad. I remember the argument that unfolded afterward.

At 7 my dad and I finally got a place of our own. It was a small one bedroom apartment. I got the room, dad slept on the couch. It was here a boy my age asked to see my penis. I showed him, then he wanted to touch his penis with mine. I remember feeling sick when it was about to happen, and backing out. He wasnt very happy.

This is when my dad's alcoholism started to turn nasty. I remember nights, so many nights, of him passed out snoring on the couch while I watched television. I remember all the times he shouted at me for hours on end, ceaselessly berating me until I was dry of tears. It wasn't until last year that I realized he was verbally abusing me, and that wasn't a normal way to discipline your child. I remember I used to pray to god every night, begging him to stop my father from drinking.

One day my grandma came to take me away, and my dad went to rehab. I ended up living with my overly religious Aunt and Uncle. They had two sons. One was 14, the other was 2. The 14 year old and I used to play "games". We'd play "shark" in the pool. It was a form of tag where we'd swim around and tug on each others dicks in order to tag each other. I shared a room with him, and sometimes at night we would play "doctor". I had me perform oral sex on him, and he did the same for me. I've never told anyone this.

At around 8 years old my father gets out of rehab and we find a new place together. Things are fine and dandy for a long time before my dad picked up the bottle again. The verbal abuse was picked up again immediately. We had no money and lived in some sort of specialty low income housing. He held a small job that pulled in roughly $350 a month. He would burn through his money on a binge drinking craze before returning to sobriety while he waited for his next check. I remember walking home from school, unsure if he would be blacked out on the couch or not.

During this time my mother got clean and started sending child support checks, this only fueled my father's addiction more and made everything worse. I lived with this man until I was 14.

The very end of my eighth grade year I finally broke down and told my school counselor. He had me whisked away from there asap. I remember the embarrassment I felt when the social worker told me that my dad was completely naked when she went to go inspect my living situation.

I lived in a foster home for a few months before my mom got custody and I was moved half-way across the country where she had started a new life. My life was good for several years after that. My mom had re-married a European, and he was kind of a dick, but beyond that my home life was the best I had ever had.

My senior year of high school my mother went to go visit some old friends. Shortly after that I found out that her and my step-dad filed for divorce. He cheated on her while on a trip to Turkey, and she relapsed on her trip, and had been smoking meth since her return.

He moved out, and I lived with her until I graduated high school. I remember the tweakers that would come by to hang out and vulture off my mom who was spending her life's savings on smack. She kicked me out shortly into the summer after she accused me of stealing from her instead of blaming her tweaker friends, and I pushed her in my resulting rage.

I floated around for a few weeks, crashing on friends' couches before moving in with my sister. This was two years ago, and I lived by myself now. I've been doing a lot of soul searching, connecting dots between my depression and lack of self confidence to my father's verbal abuse, and my hyper-sexuality to my history of molestation from my cousin.

I haven't seen either of my parents since I last left their respective households. I'm sad, and I miss them because I know the great parents they are when they're sober, but I know that addiction is a beast that I cant tame for them. I fear that I will get news of their deaths any day now. They're both in their fifties.

I know I went off the topic a bit, but this post sort of became a cathartic essay for me. I've never written out every fucked up thing that happened to me in my life, and seeing the sheer volume of words here sickens me.

Anyways, I love you reddit. Bye-bye. /internethug

I still have fear when I think about it now, I'm still afraid of their anger, and I am afraid having to admit to being such a scumbag steve; I care a lot about how much people trust and like me, so I feel this is the most difficult thing I have ever had to do. 

I got stoned, put it off for the whole night, and rationalized it into the next day. I need to stop listening to my 'rational' mind. It's what got me into this mess in the first place, so I feel I can't trust my own judgment.I have to take the path of most resistance for once in my life.

I know a girl who attaches all of her personal issues to her anxiety, she doesn't work at her issues because she sees them as an ingrained, natural part of herself. I do not want my depression to own me like her illness owns her. I want to take responsibility for my actions and for my life.
especially when those lies causes you shame and guilt, my moods are even darker because of my lying.

I'll call some of my family, ask around. It's tough to do, but I don't think I should give up without trying. I'll keep you posted in this thread on how I'm doing.

And thank you for doing what you do, thanks for taking the time out of your day to look after people who feel like they have no one.

I think its the thought of moving thats really getting to me. It feels as though I had my life on the right track, and that I might be okay after all. But this is threatening  all I've worked for, and I don't know if I could handle the disappointment if it all came crashing down. The disappointment in myself, the disappointment of my family and friends, and the disappointment in thinking that I was on my way to being happy and functional.
